1  JUDGMENT
This petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of M.V.Act, 1989 claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- in respect of accidental injuries sustained by him in the Road Traffic Accident.

2. In the petition it is stated that, on 31.05.2023 at about 6.30 pm petitioner was traveling in Autorikshaw bearing Regn No. KA-05-AL-5990 as inmate along with his friend Ashok from Kengeri towards Subbarayappanapalya on Mysore road.

When they reached near BMTC depot cross Kengeri, the driver of said Autorikshaw drove the said vehicle in a rash and negligent manner without observing traffic rules and regulations and while taking turn he lost control over the Autorikshaw, therefore the Auto rolled over and accident is caused.

The petitioner has sustained severe injuries and he was shifted to Supra hospital, Kengeri, wherein he took conservative treatment and discharged on same day and on the next day ie., 01-06-2023 he suffered hectic pain and again went to the Supra hospital wherein, x-ray was conducted and it is found that he sustained fracture of left clavicle.
He underwent surgery, internal fixation was done and (SCCH-12) 3 MVC.No.3646/2023 he was discharged on 03-06-2023 with the advice to take regular followup treatment.
The accidental injuries sustained by the petitioner are due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Autorikshaw.

3. It is further stated in the petition that due to the accident petitioner suffered loss of income, he was aged about 32 years and working under one licenced civil contractor by name Sri Manjunath and thereby earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries he cannot do any work now and cannot ride two wheeler and therefore he sustained permanent disability.
Kengeri traffic police have registered case in Crime No. 180/2023 against the driver of the aforesaid Autorikshaw for the offences punishable U/Sec.279 and 338 of IPC.
1st respondent is R.C owner and 2nd respondent is insurance company of the vehicle of 1st respondent and they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
On all these grounds he prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest in the above case.
4. On issuance of notice, respondent no.1 owner is served.
He remained absent on the date of hearing hence he is placed exparte.
Respondent 2 appeared through his counsel and filed written statement stating that petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts and it is liable to be dismissed in limine.

He admitted the issuance of commercial vehicle package policy in respect of Autorikshaw bearing Regn No.KA-05-AL- 5990 and it is valid from 06-11-2022 to 05-11-2023 and his liability is strictly in terms and conditions of the insurance (SCCH-12) 4 MVC.No.3646/2023 policy.
That 1st respondent has violated Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of IMV Act.
Police was failed to inform the insurance company about the incident and there was delay of 4 days in filing the complaint and the same is only to cause wrongful loss to the 2 nd respondent.
Involvement of the vehicle and injuries sustained by the petitioner are denied, medical treatment taken and expenses incurred which were alleged by the petitioner are denied.

The driver of Auto was not holding license and its owner has entrusted the vehicle to the person who did not possess valid driving license and therefore 2 nd respondent is not liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
That the occurrence of the accident as explained by the petitioner is denied.
Age, occupation and income of the petitioner and permanent disability are denied.

That the compensation amount claimed by the petitioner is Raghu.H vs Muneera on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25062086/
2 highly excessive, exorbitant and fanciful.
On all these grounds he prayed to dismiss the claim petition.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, I have framed following:-
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that on 31-05- 2023 at about 6.30 PM he was travelling in Autorikshaw bearing Regn No.KA-05-AL-5990 along with his friend Ashok near BMTC Depot cross, Kengeri, the driver of Autorikshaw driven the said vehicle in high speed and in rash and negligent manner and while taking turn Autorikshaw rolled over and caused accident and petitioner sustained grievous injuries as alleged?
(SCCH-12) 5 MVC.No.3646/2023 2.
Whether the petitioner proves his age, occupation, income and permanent disability if any?

3. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation If so by whom and what is the quantum?
4. What Order or Award?
6. To prove his case, petitioner is examined as P.W.1.
Ex.P.1 to P.10 documents are marked on his behalf.
M.R.O of Supra hospital is examined as P.W.2 and through him Ex.P.11 to 15 documents are marked.
One Doctor by name Avinash Parthasarathy is examined as P.W.3 through him Ex.P.16 to 18 documents are marked.
All of them were fully cross examined.
On the other hand respondent no.2 has not lead any evidence.

7. Heard learned counsel for both sides on merits and perused records.
8.

On taking into consideration the oral and documentary evidence placed before this Tribunal and on hearing arguments, my answers to the above issues as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative, Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative, Issue No.3:
Partly in the Affirmative, Issue No.4: As per final order, for the following;
REASONS 9. ISSUE NO.1: As per the petition averments accident took place on 31.05.2023 at about 6.30 pm when petitioner was traveling in Autorikshaw bearing Regn No.KA-05-AL-5990 as (SCCH-12) 6 MVC.No.3646/2023 inmate along with his friend Ashok from Kengeri towards Subbarayappanapalya on Mysore road.

When they reached near BMTC depot cross Kengeri, the driver of said Autorikshaw drove the said vehicle in a rash and negligent manner without observing traffic rules and regulations and while taking turn he lost control over the Autorikshaw as such, the Raghu.
H vs Muneera on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25062086/
3 Auto rolled over and accident is caused by which petitioner sustained severe injuries as alleged in the petition.
10. To prove his case petitioner entered in to witness box, and got examined as PW.1 and he reiterated the petition averments in his chief examination.

To prove involvement of vehicle and negligence on part of driver of Autorikshaw petitioner has produced FIR at Cr.No.180/2023, first information, spot panchanama, rough sketch, IMV report, wound certificate, final report and discharge summary which are marked at Ex.P1 to P8.

Petitioner himself has given first information to police on 03-6-2023 i.e, after 3 days of the accident stating that, while he was traveling in aforesaid Autorikshaw, the driver of said Auto was negligent and petitioner sustained injuries due to the said accident.
Further the driver of Autorikshaw stated that he would pay the medical expenses but he did not pay it.
Therefore police complaint is given on 03-06-2023 after lapse of 3 days of the accident.
On the basis of said first information Kengeri Traffic Police have registered at Cr.No.180/2023 against the driver of the Autorikshaw for the offences punishable U/Sec.279 and 338 of IPC.
On investigation they have filed charge sheet against the same driver for the offences punishable (SCCH-12) 7 MVC.No.3646/2023 U/Sec.279, 337 and 338 of IPC.

In the wound certificate it is mentioned that petitioner was admitted with the history of RTA alleged to have occurred on 31-05-2023 and he sustained fracture of left clavical and abrasion over the fore head.
According to the doctor injury No.1 was grievous and injury No.2 was simple in nature.
IMV report shows that, the said Autorikshaw sustained damages on its front side and left side and also the rubbing marks were found and accident was not due to any mechanical defect in the vehicle.
As per the spot mahazar it can be seen that road was 40 feet wide tar road.
One Ashok who is eye witness to the incident has shown the spot.
He is also victim of the accident as per the final report.
FIR and final report shows the involvement of autorickshaw in the accident.
The owner has not challenged the involvement of his vehicle in this accident.
Driver also not questioned case filed against him by the police.

As per the wound certificate injury sustained by the petitioner are due to the accident caused on 31.05.2023 and the history mentioned by the petitioner are not said to be false by the respondent side in the cross examination of P.W.1 the manner of accident is explained by the petitioner in the first information as well as in the cross examination of P.w.1,
Though the manner of accident is denied, 2nd respondent has no other satisfactory explanation in respect of injuries sustained by the petitioner otherwise from the accident.
Respondent side has not given evidence in respect of negligence nor the driver of auto is summoned to give evidence on the point of negligence.

Therefore, in the opinion of this court as per the police documents and medical records, the injuries sustained' (SCCH-12) 8 MVC.No.3646/2023 by the petitioner are caused due to accident occurred on 31.05.2023 by rash and negligent driving of the driver of autorickshaw bearing reg.No.KA-05-AC-5990 in the above case.
Accordingly, I hold this Issue in the Affirmative.
11. ISSUE NO.2 : To prove his age petitioner in the petition it is stated that petitioner is aged 32 years, but no I.D proofs are produced.
In cross examination of P.W.1 he stated that he was born on 10.08.1991.
Accident took place on 31.05.2023.
He was aged 31 years at the time of accident and not completed 32 years.
Therefore, the age of the petitioner is considered as 31 years at the time of accident Raghu.
H vs Muneera

on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25062086/
4 12.
In respect of occupation it is stated that, petitioner is Civil Sub-contractor working under one licenced Civil contractor by name Manjunatha.

It is stated that petitioner was earning Rs.30,000/-
per month.
To prove this fact he has not produced any document.
Therefore, notional income has to be considered.
The accident took place in the year 2023 and Petitioner being resident of Bengaluru

,
it is proper to consider his income at Rs.16,000/- per month.

Hence monthly income of the petitioner is held as Rs.16,000/-.
13.
In respect of permanent disability a doctor by name Avinash Parthasarathy is examined as P.W.3.
He is Consultant- Orthopedic Surgeon working at Srinivasa hospital, Balepete.
Bengaluru.

The said Doctor has assessed the disability of petitioner on 23.05.2024 and found tenderness over left clavical, restriction in arc movement, difficulty in carrying over his activities and old left clavicle fracture with implants in situ.
As per the evidence of doctor petitioner suffers total disability of 10% of the whole body.
It is settled law that, doctor can only assess physical disability and cannot assess the functional disability having regard to avocation of the patient.
In the cross examination of P.W.3, such assessment made by the doctor is disputed by the 2nd respondent.
He relied upon the judgment in Jayanth Kumar.

B V/s M.J.Mahesh, MFA 1602/2016 Dt.29.06.2016 passed by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in which, it is held the clavical bone is only ornamental bone and the fracture to it does not lead to any disability.
In the present case, except clavicle bone fracture there is no other injury was sustained by the petitioner.

Therefore, the decision relied by the 2nd respondent is applicable to the present case and no functional disability can be attributed to the petitioner having regard to his avocation Civil Sub-contractor.
Accordingly I answer this issue Partly in the Affirmative.
14. ISSUE NO.3 :
In view of above reasons, injuries sustained by petitioner are due to the accident caused by the driver of the Autorikshaw bearing Regn No.KA-05-AL-5990.
There is nexus between the injuries sustained by the petitioner and the accident.
Hence he is entitled to compensation at the hands of respondents.

The quantum of compensation is determined as under:
(i) For Pain and sufferings: The petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
The records show that he underwent operation and implants are in situ.
He was in hospital for (SCCH-12) 10 MVC.No.3646/2023 01.06.2023 to 03.06.2023 as per discharge summary produced at Ex.
P.8 with advice to take complete rest, continue medicine and to take follow up treatment
. Therefore, for pain and suffering the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/- .
(ii) For Medical expenses:
The petitioner has produced medical bills at Ex.P.9.
Totally he has paid amount of Rs.71,938/- as per Ex.P.9 medical bills.
The said payment of bill is due to the accident caused to him.
They are subsequent to the date of accident.
Though they are disputed, no satisfactory material is placed to disbelieve the bills.
Therefore, petitioner is entitled for medical expenses of Rs.71,938/-.

Raghu.H vs Muneera on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25062086/
5 (iii) For Food and nourishment:
The petitioner was admitted to Supra hospital on 01.06.2023 and discharged on 03.06.2023.
He was in hospital for 03 days .
Accident took place in the year 2023.
Since he was in hospital, food and nourishment charges will have to be awarded.
Considering the cost of living, and food, nourishment charges if per day Rs.500/- is awarded it will meet the ends of justice.
Hence for food and nourishment Rs.500/- x 03 days = Rs. 1,500/-is awarded.
(iv) For Attendant charges:
For a period of inpatient for 03 days some one should have looked after petitioner in the hospital.
Even if his family member has taken care of him in the said period, that family member's income for those days is lost.
Hence per day if Rs.500/- is awarded as attendant charges in 2023, it will meet the ends of justice.
Hence for attendant charges Rs.500/- x 03 days =Rs.1,500/-is awarded.
For Loss of income during laid up period:
As per the finding to issue No.2, the income of the petitioner per month is. Rs.16,000/-.
He was inpatient for 03 days and he was advised to take rest also5 as he has underwent operation.
Minimum 2 months is required to recover from such operation in view of grievous injury.

Therefore, laid up period of petitioner is considered as total 2 months including in patient period and loss of income during laid up period is Rs.16,000/-x 2=
32,000/-
He is entitled to Rs.32,000/- as loss of income during laid up period.
(vi) Conveyance charges:
It is stated that petitioner was shifted to Supra hospital from the spot of accident.
He is further required to go for one more surgery for removal of implants.
He has spent money for conveyance for the purpose of treatment.
Considering all those conveyances, in the opinion of this tribunal if an amount of Rs.5,000/- is awarded it will meet the ends of justice.
(vii) Loss of future income due to Disability : As per the findings given to issue no.2 there is no functional disability of the petitioner due to which he may loose income.
Hence, no compensation is awarded towards loss of future income due to disability.
(viii) Physical discomfort and loss of amenities of life :

As per the evidence of assessed doctor,
petitioner complained about pain and difficulty in carrying out overhead activities due to clavicle bone fracture as such he suffers discomfort.
Meaning, he cannot lead the normal life as he used to live before the accident.
Certainly accident has caused physical discomfort and came in the way of normal enjoyment of life.
Hence in the opinion of this court, petitioner is entitled to compensation under the head of physical discomfort and loss of amenities of life.
Under the said head he is entitled for Rs.30,000/-
(ix) For Future medical expenses: P.W.3 has stated that petitioner is in need of one more surgery for removal of implants.
Removal of implant is necessary for well being of the petitioner.
According to doctor minimum 35 thousand is necessary for removal of implant.
No estimation is submitted in that regard.

Hence, in the opinion of this court amount of Rs.25,000/- is sufficient for removal of Raghu.H vs Muneera on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25062086/
6 implants.
Accordingly, Rs.25,000/- is awarded under this head.

Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:-
 Particulars of Heads In Rs.
i. Pain & Sufferings 30,000/-
ii.

Medical expenses 71,938/-
iii. Food and nourishment 1,500/-
iv. Attendant charges 1,500/-
v. Loss of income during laid up 32,000/-
 period vi.

Conveyance charges 5,000/-
vii. Loss of income due to disability NIL viii Physical discomfort and loss of 30,000/-
 amenities of life ix.

Future medical expenses 25,000/-
 (SCCH-12) 13 MVC.No.3646/2023
Therefore, I hold that the petitioner is entitled for a total compensation of Rs.1,96,938/- in respect of injuries sustained by him in the Road traffic accident.
15. Liability: Since Respondent no.2 has admitted the insurance policy, he is liable to indemnify the insured.
Hence, I answer this issue "Partly in the Affirmative".
16. ISSUE NO.4:-

In view of above reasons I proceed to pass following :
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner u/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
It is held that, petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.1,96,938/- with interest @ 6% pa on the amount of Rs.1,71,938/- from the date of petition till the date of payment.
(Future medical expenses of Rs.25,000/- will not carry interest).
The respondent no.2 insurance company is liable to indemnify the insured and directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount with interest within one month from the date of this order.

Raghu.H vs Muneera on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25062086/
7 (SCCH-12) 14 MVC.No.3646/2023
After such deposit, the petitioner is entitled to have release of entire compensation along with interest without making F.D.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Award be drawn accordingly.
